GraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale: Facts verified 2026-11-22 in the worktree on spec/release-rewrite-boundary (main = bb68fd6c). The annotated tag v2.8.2 targets commit 3b6d49e4e4a15452aced6cb25793446edf8d1c7e with tree fcc46b7ba481d886d3e3d497af634337246c12f7; `git merge-base --is-ancestor` proves that commit is NOT an ancestor of main, and no commit in main history carries the tag tree. The history rewrite of 2026-10-28 severed the recorded release line from current main, so the manifest rule bootstrapSha = commit pins the strict boundary to a commit that cannot be an ancestor of any future payload. The nearest current-history commit is 16a4a47ed723740e330e44cf448bcbada766882c (PR #63, 2026-10-25), an ancestor of main; `git diff --name-only v2.8.2 16a4a47e` is exactly 81 paths — 72 under site/, 8 under tests/, 1 = .github/workflows/site.yml — and none matches the product prefixes or product files, which is what makes the deltaPaths proof meaningful here. Current tool behavior (tools/release-readiness.mjs, lines 769-786): the tag target check fails with MT_RELEASE_PREVIOUS_BOUNDARY_INVALID (tagCommit=...;recorded=...), the tag/bootstrap tree check fails with 'tree=drift', and `git merge-base --is-ancestor bootstrapSha payload` fails with 'bootstrap=not-ancestor'; validateCommitAccounting (lines 320-398) pins commitAccounting.fromExclusive to previousRelease.bootstrapSha. The change replaces only the bootstrap tree leg of 'tree=drift' with the historyRewrite delta proof when bootstrapSha differs from commit; the tag tree leg, ancestry and accounting stay as-is. Keeping commit and tree pointed at the real tag preserves the honest statement "this train continues exactly release v2.8.2", while bootstrapSha honestly says "accounting starts at this current-history commit, and here is the complete non-product delta between them".

Alternatives.Alternative: Rejected: rewrite main again so a commit with the tag tree exists — falsifies published history and violates the no-rewrite rule of this change.

Rejected: create an anchor tag on a current-history commit with an equivalent tree and point the manifest at it — invents a tag that was never released and still does not prove the recorded v2.8.2 boundary.
Rejected: merge the pre-rewrite line into main to restore ancestry — pollutes the product history line with the abandoned one and is explicitly forbidden.

Rejected: relax or drop the strict boundary proof — weakens a fail-closed release gate; this change keeps every existing failure and only replaces the bootstrap tree leg with a stricter, path-level proof.

Rejected: prove the delta by tree hashes alone (commit tree vs recorded tree) — a tree hash equality claim cannot enumerate which non-product paths were added, so a product change could hide inside a "matching" bootstrap; deltaPaths gives the exact path list and confines it.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Exact rejection message tokens for a missing/malformed historyRewrite (the code MT_RELEASE_PREVIOUS_BOUNDARY_INVALID is fixed by the spec; the message detail is a plan-time choice consistent with existing 'tree=drift'/'bootstrap=not-ancestor' style).

Whether the existing strictRepository fixture migrates via an explicit empty-delta historyRewrite ({ date, deltaPaths: [] }) or by pinning its bootstrapSha to the tagged baseline commit; both satisfy the spec.
Exact names of the new named constants for the product prefix and product file lists and their module map wording.
Whether the optional historyRewrite field requires a TRAIN_SCHEMA_VERSION bump is assumed not to (Assumption 2 of the spec); owner confirms at approval.

Scenarios.Scenario: After this change lands, a separate train bookkeeping commit (out of scope here) fills previousRelease in docs/release-trains/2.9.x-next.json with bootstrapSha = 16a4a47ed723740e330e44cf448bcbada766882c and historyRewrite = { date: 2026-10-28, deltaPaths: [the 81 sorted non-product paths] }, keeping commit = 3b6d49e4e4a15452aced6cb25793446edf8d1c7e and tree = fcc46b7ba481d886d3e3d497af634337246c12f7; from then on the train can pass Frozen strict validation and reach Ready without weakening any other gate.
Any later drift between the recorded deltaPaths and the real tag-to-bootstrap diff (for example after another history rewrite) fails closed with rewrite=delta-drift before the train can be frozen.
If someone tries to smuggle a product path into the recorded delta, the product-drift rejection fires even though the diff itself matches, keeping the release payload boundary product-only.
